speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Twopence the letter, sixpence the parcel, and nothing at all for what you shout after me down the yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have shouted nothing. I have eightpence, the parcel, and the question with it.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I brought it from the house, brother. The knot is at the side. She was particular.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Particular is free. Sixpence is the parcel. Let me see the knot.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Oiled cloth. It is meant to arrive, not to be looked at.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: It will do. A horse will not take it for a cheese if the knot is dull.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: They are sound. I looked at the feet. You know I do.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: The ruts are iron from here to the hill. I walked the last mile in. I do not trot a beast on iron.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six horses, and all of them walked in.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Six. I count them before I count your money. They drink before I talk of bags.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Pay him, brother. He is happier with the coin than with a speech about the road.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sixpence the parcel. Twopence the letter. There. Eightpence.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Eightpence. I have it. The parcel goes north on this load.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The letter asks one question. It does not need a speech wrapped round it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: I can carry the letter. I cannot make her read what you meant instead.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: The direction is Henley Street. You have carried that door often enough.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Often enough to know it. Twelve hours to Wycombe if the way's dry. It is not dry. It is iron. Name it longer, and do not shout a second direction after me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No second direction. Anne Shakespeare, Henley Street. The question is inside.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: I water them before I turn a bag out. You will not have me sorting in the yard with six beasts still cold.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Water them. I am not in a hurry to stand in this wind.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nor I. The throat is worse than it was at two. The play is done. The parcel is yours.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: The play is no business of a horse. The parcel is. I have the eightpence, and I have the direction.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Go home, brother. You are no use to a horse, and the wind is making a sermon of you.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: He is a delay on an iron day. I have the money. We are done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: We are done. I will not keep them standing.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I will see them drink, and then I am for St Bride's. Do not wait on me.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Nobody waits. The inward bags stay shut till the water is done. That is the whole of my news.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I have none to carry back but the eightpence gone. Good night to the road.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Good night. Do not shout.
